assumptions.text: No task assignee/candidate group documented; the four user tasks are left unassigned (same gap as SR-3).

Branch precedence and default are undocumented (D03 ¶93–115): nothing says which flag wins if several are true, or what happens if none is. All four flags default to null (D03 ¶66–69). Conditions are emitted in document order with no default flow.

Flag reset on loop-back is undocumented (D03 ¶102–103, ¶112–113): nothing clears isAddEmployee / isAddSubcontractor when a search screen returns, so the same branch is taken again unless the form resets the flag.

The merged return flows carry no condition, so empCancel and SubconCancel are set but never read: of the 3 cancel paths D03 ¶225 counts, only allocationCancel is routed. Cancelling the employee search is documented as returning without selection (D04 ¶251); for the subcontractor search D04 ¶265 says only that the flag is set. Nothing in the process enforces either.

assumptions.text: Write contents are only partly documented. D03 ¶126 lists updatedBy and updatedOn among the fields of each written employee record, but the screen initialises only employee, project, createdBy, createdOn and isActive (D03 ¶140–145), D05 ¶343–344 sets updatedBy/updatedOn on record update, and D02 ¶287 says all four audit fields are captured at allocation time. The list written is existing rows merged with new ones (D03 ¶146), so the write is an upsert; whether soft-deleted rows reach it is not stated. Nothing is documented for the subcontractor records beyond D03 ¶130. Both lists default to null (D03 ¶64–65) and both writes are unconditional.

assumptions.text: Lifecycle settings are not carried: GMT+12, archive 7 days after completion, delete 7 days after archival, no notifications (D03 ¶50–54).
empCancel and SubconCancel are documented as internal, not parameters (D03 ¶70–71); the spec declares all variables alike.
